entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Euthalius was a deacon of Alexandria and later Bishop of Sulca; he is chiefly known through his work on the New Testament in particular as the author of the 'Euthalian Apparatus'.

Euthalius lived during the 4th century AD, a period marked by significant religious and cultural upheaval in the Roman Empire. He was part of the Alexandrian school of biblical scholars, which sought to reconcile Christian theology with Jewish scripture.

The Euthalian Apparatus, a critical apparatus for the New Testament, demonstrates Euthalius' expertise in biblical exegesis and his efforts to establish a standardized system for interpreting Scripture. This work had a lasting impact on Christian biblical studies, influencing subsequent scholars such as Jerome and Augustine.

Euthalius' legacy extends beyond his own time, as his work reflects the cultural exchange and intellectual currents of the late antique world. His contributions to the field of New Testament scholarship continue to be studied by historians and theologians today.
